Package frc.robot.util

Class AdvantageUtil

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.util.AdvantageUtil
public final class AdvantageUtil extends Object
Utility class providing convenient methods for working with AdvantageKit and mode-dependent code.

This class is never instantiated and provides static methods for:

  • Selecting implementations based on the current robot mode (real vs replay)
  • Logging active commands for debugging and analysis

All methods here should use AdvantageConstants.kCurrentMode to determine the runtime environment.

  • Method Details

    • match

      public static <T> T match(T real, T replay)
      Selects between two implementations based on the current robot mode.

      Used to choose between real robot implementations and replay/simulation alternatives. For example, this could select between a hardware-based gyro and a logged gyro replay.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of the implementation objects
      Parameters:
      real - The implementation to use when running on a real robot
      replay - The implementation to use when replaying from logs
      Returns:
      The selected implementation based on the current mode
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the mode is Sim (which is not supported)

    • match

      public static <T> T match(Supplier<T> real, Supplier<T> replay)
      Selects between two implementations provided as suppliers based on the current robot mode.

      This version is useful when the implementations are expensive to create and should only be instantiated when selected. The appropriate supplier is called to create the instance.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The type of the implementation objects
      Parameters:
      real - A supplier that creates the real robot implementation
      replay - A supplier that creates the replay implementation
      Returns:
      The selected implementation instance based on the current mode

    • logActiveCommand

      public static void logActiveCommand(edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem self)
      Logs the currently active command for a given subsystem.

      This is useful for debugging to understand which command is controlling a subsystem at any given time. The active command name is logged to AdvantageKit under the subsystem's "ActiveCommand" property.

      Parameters:
      self - The subsystem to log the active command for
